llm.domain: Culture Ontology. Single sentences extracted from Wikipedia articles.

Dance.description: An entity of the type "dance", as defined by the Culture Ontology.

name.description: The text that identifies this Dance in the source text.
name.instructions: Use the exact surface form as it appears in the source text, without adding, removing, reordering or normalizing any words.

indigenous_to.description: The "indigenous to" of this Dance, as defined by the Culture Ontology.
indigenous_to.instructions: Only fill this field when the source text explicitly states it; otherwise leave it empty. Each value must use the exact surface form as it appears in the source text, without normalizing its words. When the text states several values, for instance as an enumeration, extract each value on its own and separate them with ";": "written for violin, cello and piano" gives "violin; cello; piano".

Festival.description: An entity of the type "festival", as defined by the Culture Ontology.

name.description: The text that identifies this Festival in the source text.
name.instructions: Use the exact surface form as it appears in the source text, without adding, removing, reordering or normalizing any words.
examples: Nelson Mandela: An International Tribute for a Free South Africa

start_time.description: The "start time" of this Festival, as defined by the Culture Ontology.
start_time.instructions: Only fill this field when the source text explicitly states it; otherwise leave it empty. Each value must use the exact surface form as it appears in the source text, without normalizing its words. When the text states several values, for instance as an enumeration, extract each value on its own and separate them with ";": "written for violin, cello and piano" gives "violin; cello; piano". Dates must be written in the format "<DD> <Month> <YYYY>". When the source text states only a year, use "01 January <YYYY>".
